entity_types: publichna organizatsiia (public organization), fundatsiia (foundation), publichno-koristna (public-benefit) status
local_requirements: Organization 2+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Ukrainian-language documents (English with certified translation); state-fee registration online.
cost_time: State duty ~1,000-2,500 UAH + translations/notary; ~1-2 weeks (online filing)
notes: Registration itself is cheap and fast, but active war, banking/sanctions friction for a foreign resident founder and currency risk make this a risky base; many Western expat charities run via local Ukrainian partners.

entity_types: publicnaya organizatsiya (public organization), fundatsiya (foundation)
local_requirements: Nominally 5+ members for an organization (foreigners allowed in statute), local office, Belarusian-language charter; in practice foreign-funded NGOs above a funding threshold must register as 'undesirable organizations' before operating.
cost_time: Nominally low fees, 1-3 months; in practice effectively barred for an independent foreign founder
notes: 2021+ crackdown on independent civil society; heavy political risk; private foundations rare and state-dominated; not recommended for this founder.

entity_types: asociație (association), fundație (foundation)
local_requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local office, Romanian-language statute; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed.
cost_time: ~500 RON state fee + notary ~1,000-2,000 RON; ~1-3 months (statutory 30 days)
notes: EU member; moderate bureaucracy; 'de utilitate publică' (public-benefit) tax status is a separate, stricter procedure; English support OK in Bucharest/Cluj.

entity_types: shtoprofitna asotsiia (public-benefit association), neprofitna pravno lice (nonprofit legal entity), fondatsiya (foundation)
local_requirements: Nonprofit legal entity (NPL) needs only 1 founder (foreigners allowed) + local office; association needs 5+ founders; Bulgarian-language documents.
notes: EU member; the 1-founder NPL form is the simplest for a lone foreign founder; good English support in Sofia; cheap to operate.

entity_types: syndesmos (association, general-benefit status), themelioma (foundation)
local_requirements: Association needs 5+ founders (foreigners allowed), Greek registered office, Greek-language charter filed with notary and court registry; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed.
notes: 2019 law modernized foundations, but process is paper/notary-heavy, Greek language required, no meaningful online registry; use a local lawyer.

entity_types: charitable trust (unregistered), registered body (association), community chest
local_requirements: A charitable trust needs only a settlor + trustee and no registration; registered body needs 3+ members (foreigners allowed) + local address; English fully accepted.
cost_time: Trust: ~500-2,000 EUR via solicitor, days; registered body: ~100-500 EUR, ~2-6 weeks
notes: English common-law jurisdiction — most expats set up a simple charitable trust with a Cypriot trustee; tax deductibility requires income-tax authority approval and a Cypriot public-benefit nexus; strong English-language professional services.

entity_types: association (2021 Non-Not-For-Profit Organisations Act), foundation, charitable trust
local_requirements: Association 3+ founders (foreigners allowed), local registered address; foundation 1 founder, endowment per charter, notary deed; English fully accepted.
cost_time: Association ~150-500 EUR, ~days-2 weeks (online); foundation ~1,500-5,000 EUR, ~2-6 weeks
notes: English official language, streamlined 2021 framework; foundation is the stronger form for asset-holding; charitable trusts available under trust law without registration.

entity_types: amuta (registered association), nonprofit corporation (amuta atzmit), public-benefit corporation (charitable amuta with DSD status)
local_requirements: 2-3 founders over 18 (Israeli citizenship NOT required), local Israeli registered agent/office, attorney-filed founding declaration and bylaws; English widely accepted
notes: One of the most foreign-friendly registration regimes in the region; most foreign founders use an amuta plus a local managing director and registered-agent service; English-language filings routinely accepted; charity tax status (DSD/13-b) is a separate follow-up application

entity_types: registered association (jam'iyya) with Ministry of Social Affairs, charitable trust (less common)
local_requirements: Board members must be Jordanian citizens, 18+, fully competent; Jordanian local address; Arabic documents; foreign founder can only be a non-board supporter
cost_time: A$100-500 fees, 1-3 months (gated by finding 5+ Jordanian-citizen board members)
notes: Most foreigners fund through established Jordanian charities (e.g. JRC) or a branch/representative office instead of forming; government approval of bylaws and activities required; English not required in filings

entity_types: association (jama'iyya) under Law 92/1996, private foundation (muassasa khassisa)
local_requirements: Foreigners CAN be founders and directors (no nationality rule) but need a local registered office, Arabic founding documents, and a local signatory; notification (declaration) regime, not pre-approval
notes: Legally one of the easiest for foreigners in the region, but heavy Arabic-only bureaucracy, bank-account opening friction, and macro instability (currency, banking) make practical setup harder; most internationals use a local registered partner or a foundation

entity_types: association registered with Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor, private foundation
local_requirements: Local registration, local address and signatories; new association regime post-2025 is still being implemented; in-person steps in Syria; OFAC sanctions complicate cross-border funding and US-dollar transactions
cost_time: Nominally low fees, 1-4 months in a stable environment; currently not practically achievable remotely
notes: Civil-society registration resumed after 2025 transition (586 NGOs registered by Feb 2025) but framework unstable; sanctions exposure for foreign founders and their banks; English support effectively unavailable; advise against direct formation

entity_types: NGO/association (jam'iyya) under Law 12/2010, private foundation, branch of international NGO
local_requirements: Founding members must be Iraqi nationals or Iraq-resident; minimum 10 founders; local board, local address; Arabic filings; activity approvals from MoSAL
notes: Resident-expat route is the standard workaround (Iraqi-resident staff as founders); foreign funding rules restrict donor channels; English commonly understood in NGO sector but filings in Arabic; security considerations for in-person steps

entity_types: civil society organization (association) under the 2024 Civil Society Law, branch of foreign NGO (via partnership)
local_requirements: At least 10 founding members, ALL Saudi citizens; Saudi board; Saudi address; no foreign-founded charities; foreigners may only join as members of an existing Saudi organization
cost_time: N/A for foreign founder (formation not permitted); partnership route: several months
notes: New 2024 law (Royal Decree M/111) modernized the regime but kept the Saudi-citizenship floor; the only realistic foreign route is a program partnership with a Saudi charity or a representative office for an existing foreign NGO; English widely used in government dealings

entity_types: association (jam'iyya) under the NGOs Law, representative office of foreign NGO
local_requirements: Founders and board must be Kuwaiti citizens; local address; Arabic filings; foreign individuals cannot form an NGO
cost_time: N/A for foreign founder (formation not permitted); representative-office route: 2-4 months with a local partner
notes: Closed to foreign formation; foreigners work through established Kuwaiti charities (e.g. Kuwait Foundation for the Disabled, local societies) or a government-approved representative office; English usable informally, filings in Arabic

entity_types: private charitable institution (Qatar Charity framework), branch/partnership with an existing charity
local_requirements: Founding of a charitable institution requires Qatari citizens (Qatari chair and majority); foreign founders cannot establish a standalone charity; English filings accepted by many agencies
cost_time: N/A for foreign founder (standalone formation not permitted); partnership route: 1-3 months
notes: 2023 philanthropy law tightened state oversight of foreign-funded work; standard foreign route is a partnership with Qatar Charity or an established Doha NGO, or a representative office approved by the relevant ministry

entity_types: private foundation (charitable) under Federal Decree-Law 11/2018, registered charity (DCC/DED charity license), association (jama'iyya) under FDL 2/2019
local_requirements: Foundation: 1-3 founders, 100% foreign ownership allowed, AED 100,000+ capital, local service provider; association: board must be at least 70% UAE nationals; local office address; English accepted
cost_time: Foundation: AED 30,000-75,000 all-in (capital + fees + agent), 4-8 weeks; DCC charity registration for an existing foreign charity: AED 5,000-15,000, 4-8 weeks
notes: Most accessible Gulf option for a foreign founder: a UAE private foundation can be 100% foreign-held and run charitable activities; Dubai Charities (DCC) also registers existing international charities; the association route is blocked for all-foreign boards by the 70% nationality rule; strong English-language support

entity_types: association (jama'iyya), private foundation, branch of foreign NGO
local_requirements: Founders and board majority must be Omani nationals; Omani chair; local address; Arabic filings; foreign founders cannot chair
cost_time: A$200-600 fees, 1-3 months (gated by finding Omani board members)
notes: Omani nationals are required for leadership roles; practical route for an Australian founder is a program partnership with an existing Omani charity or a representative office with a local sponsor; English usable in government dealings, filings in Arabic

entity_types: association (NGO) under Law 19/2006, branch of international NGO
local_requirements: Founders must be Bahraini citizens (min. ~20) and board must be at least two-thirds Bahraini; local address; Arabic filings
cost_time: A$200-500 fees, 4-8 weeks (gated by Bahraini board)
notes: Bahrain is the most English-friendly and transparent NGO administration in the Gulf, but the nationality floor on founders/board keeps foreign formation out of reach; standard route is a partnership with an existing Bahraini NGO; government relations are comparatively accessible

entity_types: association (jama'iyya) under NGO Law 73/1991, NGO representative office (MOU-based)
local_requirements: Registration with Ministry of Social Affairs, local address and local signatories; in-person steps; operating environment requires MOU with authorities
cost_time: N/A in practice; formal route nominally 1-3 months in a stable environment, not feasible given the conflict
notes: Civil war, fragmented governance, sanctions (Yemen Sanctions) and funding restrictions make direct foreign formation impractical; all foreign work runs through humanitarian MOUs with recognized authorities and established local partners; advise against

entity_types: registered society (jam'iyya) under the 1996 Societies Law, private foundation, branch of international NGO
local_requirements: Minimum ~15 founders, two-thirds Palestinian residents of the area; local (Ramallah/West Bank) address; board majority local; Arabic filings; MoSAL registration in person
cost_time: A$150-500 fees, 2-6 weeks in a normal environment; occupation/sanctions add friction
notes: No local-partner requirement to register, so foreign participation in a society is legally possible, but in-person registration in Ramallah, movement/sanctions friction (OFAC Palestinian Territory guidelines) and banking constraints dominate; most foreigners operate via established local NGOs (e.g. PCHR, PNA partners) or international-NGO branch registration

entity_types: asociación civil (AC); fundación (Civil Code); fideicomiso (trust)
local_requirements: 3+ founders, notarized Spanish-language articles, Mexican legal address; no citizenship requirement, then SAT RFC registration.
notes: Donataria autorizada (DA) status with SAT is a separate multi-month step required for tax-deductible donations; English-speaking notary/lawyer services readily available in Mexico City.

entity_types: asociación sin fines de lucro; fundación; fideicomiso (trust)
local_requirements: Notarized Spanish articles, Guatemalan legal address, Registro de Comercio filing; foreign founders permitted.
notes: No dedicated charity registry or donor tax-benefit regime; notary and registry processes are slow; everything in Spanish.

entity_types: non-profit company (limited by guarantee); registered charity (Charities Act 2020); trust
local_requirements: 2+ directors (foreigners OK, no residency requirement), local registered office and company secretary via local agent; documents in English.
notes: English-speaking, simple Companies Registry; most expats form the non-profit company first and add charity registration later; local service providers handle everything.

entity_types: asociación sin fines de lucro; fundación (Ley 2011); fideicomiso (trust)
local_requirements: Spanish-language articles, local address, registry filing under the 2011 Associations and Foundations Law; foreign founders permitted.
notes: Donor tax benefits are limited; NGOs receiving international funds should also register in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs NGO directory.

entity_types: fundación; asociación; ONGD (registered development NGO)
local_requirements: Spanish articles, local registered office, Registro de Personas Morales plus Registro de ONGD (Chancillería) filing for NGOs.
notes: International ONGDs must register in the Registro Público de ONGD; moderate bureaucracy; all filings in Spanish.

entity_types: asociación; fundación (Ley de Fundaciones); fideicomiso (trust)
local_requirements: Spanish articles, local address, Registro Nacional filing; formally open to foreign founders.
notes: Avoid: government has dissolved 5,700+ NGO legal personalities since 2018, including foreign-funded ones; laws target foreign-financed civil society, so an Australian-founded charity faces extreme cancellation/political risk.

entity_types: asociación o fundación sin fines de lucro (single law); fideicomiso (trust)
local_requirements: Notarized Spanish articles, local registered office, Registro de Comercio; 3+ members for an asociación, single founder for a fundación.
notes: Stable, professional services widely available in English; donor tax exemption requires separate Ministry of Finance (MINFIN) approval.

entity_types: fundación de interés privado (FIP); asociación; fideicomiso (trust)
local_requirements: Spanish articles and name, local registered office, board of 3+ members, IFPF registration; single foreign founder permitted, no local nationals required.
notes: The FIP (Ley No. 8 de 2000) is the most popular expat foundation vehicle in Latin America; IFPF is a specialized fast registry; strong English-language support.
